focus.label: PMM2-congenital disorder of glycosylation
focus.description: A rare congenital disorder of N-glycosylation and is characterized by cerebellar dysfunction, abnormal fat distribution, inverted nipples, strabismus and hypotonia. 3 forms of PMM2-CDG can be distinguished: the infantile multisystem type, late-infantile and childhood ataxia-intellectual disability type (3-10 yrs old), and the adult stable disability type. Infants usually develop ataxia, psychomotor delay and extraneurological manifestations including failure to thrive, enteropathy, hepatic dysfunction, coagulation abnormalities and cardiac and renal involvement. The phenotype is however highly variable and ranges from infants who die in the first year of life to mildly involved adults.
synonyms: carbohydrate deficient glycoprotein syndrome type Ia
congenital disorder of glycosylation type Ia

notes: ClinVar / Monarch variants seen: 10 pathogenic, 5 reported

gene.function: Involved in the synthesis of the GDP-mannose and dolichol- phosphate-mannose required for a number of critical mannosyl transfer reactions. .

HP:0000218.label: High palate
HP:0000218.definition: Height of the palate more than 2 SD above the mean (objective) or palatal height at the level of the first permanent molar more than twice the height of the teeth (subjective).

ORPHA:371200.label: Congenital disorder of glycosylation with skin involvement

HP:0000486.label: Strabismus
HP:0000486.definition: A misalignment of the eyes so that the visual axes deviate from bifoveal fixation. The classification of strabismus may be based on a number of features including the relative position of the eyes, whether the deviation is latent or manifest, intermittent or constant, concomitant or otherwise and according to the age of onset and the relevance of any associated refractive error.

ORPHA:371071.label: Congenital disorder of glycosylation with epilepsy as a major feature

HP:0000582.label: Upslanted palpebral fissure
HP:0000582.lay: Upward slanting of the opening between the eyelids
HP:0000582.definition: The palpebral fissure inclination is more than two standard deviations above the mean for age (objective); or, the inclination of the palpebral fissure is greater than typical for age.

ORPHA:611314.label: Rare syndromic intellectual disability without multiple congenital anomalies/dysmorphic syndrome

HP:0001382.label: Joint hypermobility
HP:0001382.definition: The capability that a joint (or a group of joints) has to move, passively and/or actively, beyond normal limits along physiological axes.

ORPHA:371157.label: Congenital disorder of glycosylation with hepatic involvement

HP:0000154.label: Wide mouth
HP:0000154.definition: Distance between the oral commissures more than 2 SD above the mean. Alternatively, an apparently increased width of the oral aperture (subjective).

HP:0000219.label: Thin upper lip vermilion
HP:0000219.lay: Thin red part of the upper lip
HP:0000219.definition: Height of the vermilion of the upper lip in the midline more than 2 SD below the mean. Alternatively, an apparently reduced height of the vermilion of the upper lip in the frontal view (subjective).

HP:0000276.label: Long face
HP:0000276.definition: Facial height (length) is more than 2 standard deviations above the mean (objective); or, an apparent increase in the height (length) of the face (subjective).

HP:0000278.label: Retrognathia
HP:0000278.definition: An abnormality in which the mandible is mislocalised posteriorly.

HP:0000286.label: Epicanthus
HP:0000286.definition: A fold of skin starting above the medial aspect of the upper eyelid and arching downward to cover, pass in front of and lateral to the medial canthus.

HP:0000303.label: Mandibular prognathia
HP:0000303.definition: Abnormal prominence of the chin related to increased length of the mandible.

HP:0000316.label: Hypertelorism
HP:0000316.definition: Interpupillary distance more than 2 SD above the mean (alternatively, the appearance of an increased interpupillary distance or widely spaced eyes).

HP:0000343.label: Long philtrum
HP:0000343.definition: Distance between nasal base and midline upper lip vermilion border more than 2 SD above the mean. Alternatively, an apparently increased distance between nasal base and midline upper lip vermilion border.

HP:0000448.label: Prominent nose
HP:0000448.definition: Distance between subnasale and pronasale more than two standard deviations above the mean, or alternatively, an apparently increased anterior protrusion of the nasal tip.

HP:0000463.label: Anteverted nares
HP:0000463.definition: Anteriorly-facing nostrils viewed with the head in the Frankfurt horizontal and the eyes of the observer level with the eyes of the subject. This gives the appearance of an upturned nose (upturned nasal tip).

HP:0000565.label: Esotropia
HP:0000565.definition: A form of strabismus with one or both eyes turned inward ('crossed') to a relatively severe degree, usually defined as 10 diopters or more.

HP:0000750.label: Delayed speech and language development
HP:0000750.definition: A degree of language development that is significantly below the norm for a child of a specified age.

HP:0000938.label: Osteopenia
HP:0000938.definition: Osteopenia is a term to define bone density that is not normal but also not as low as osteoporosis. By definition from the World Health Organization osteopenia is defined by bone densitometry as a T score -1 to -2.5.

HP:0000939.label: Osteoporosis
HP:0000939.definition: Osteoporosis is a systemic skeletal disease characterized by low bone density and microarchitectural deterioration of bone tissue with a consequent increase in bone fragility. According to the WHO criteria, osteoporosis is defined as a BMD that lies 2.5 standard deviations or more below the average value for young healthy adults (a T-score below -2.5 SD).

HP:0001250.label: Seizure
HP:0001250.definition: A seizure is an intermittent abnormality of nervous system physiology characterized by a transient occurrence of signs and/or symptoms due to abnormal excessive or synchronous neuronal activity in the brain.

HP:0001263.label: Global developmental delay
HP:0001263.definition: A delay in the achievement of motor or mental milestones in the domains of development of a child, including motor skills, speech and language, cognitive skills, and social and emotional skills. This term should only be used to describe children younger than five years of age.

HP:0001265.label: Hyporeflexia
HP:0001265.definition: Reduction of neurologic reflexes such as the knee-jerk reaction.

HP:0001321.label: Cerebellar hypoplasia
HP:0001321.definition: Cerebellar hypoplasia is a descriptive term implying a cerebellum with a reduced volume, but a normal shape and is stable over time.

HP:0001763.label: Pes planus
HP:0001763.definition: A foot where the longitudinal arch of the foot is in contact with the ground or floor when the individual is standing; or, in a patient lying supine, a foot where the arch is in contact with the surface of a flat board pressed against the sole of the foot by the examiner with a pressure similar to that expected from weight bearing; or, the height of the arch is reduced.

HP:0001999.label: Abnormal facial shape
HP:0001999.definition: An abnormal morphology (form) of the face or its components.

HP:0002013.label: Vomiting
HP:0002013.definition: Forceful ejection of the contents of the stomach through the mouth by means of a series of involuntary spasmic contractions.

HP:0002751.label: Kyphoscoliosis
HP:0002751.definition: An abnormal curvature of the spine in both a coronal (lateral) and sagittal (back-to-front) plane.

NORD.ORG:nih-national-institute-of-arthr.label: NIH/National Institute of Arthritis and Musculoskeletal and Skin Diseases

NORD.ORG:nih-national-institute-of-neuro.label: NIH/National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke

HP:0003642.label: Type I transferrin isoform profile
HP:0003642.definition: Abnormal transferrin isoform profile consistent with a type I congenital disorder of glycosylation. In the traditional nomenclature for congenital disorders of glycosylation, absence of entire glycans was designated type I, and loss of one or more monosaccharides as type II.

HP:0000007.label: Autosomal recessive inheritance
HP:0000007.definition: A mode of inheritance that is observed for traits related to a gene encoded on one of the autosomes (i.e., the human chromosomes 1-22) in which a trait manifests in individuals with two pathogenic alleles, either homozygotes (two copies of the same mutant allele) or compound heterozygotes (whereby each copy of a gene has a distinct mutant allele).

HP:0007874.label: Almond-shaped palpebral fissure
HP:0007874.definition: A shape created by an acute downward arching of the upper eyelid and upward arching of the lower eyelid, toward the medial canthus, which gives the outline of the palpebral fissures the configuration of an almond. Thus, the maximum distance between the fissures is offset from, and medial to, the center point.

HP:0001395.label: Hepatic fibrosis
HP:0001395.definition: The presence of excessive fibrous connective tissue in the liver. Fibrosis is a reparative or reactive process.

HP:6000781.label: Reduced tissue phosphomannomutase activity
HP:6000781.definition: Activity of the enzyme phosphomannomutase (EC 5.4.2.8) in tissues below the lower limit of normal. The activity can be measured in multiple tissues including leukocytes, fibroblasts, and liver.

HP:0001251.label: Ataxia
HP:0001251.definition: Ataxia refers to impaired coordination of voluntary muscle movement. Cerebellar ataxia refers to ataxia due to dysfunction of the cerebellum. This causes a variety of elementary neurological deficits including asynergy (lack of coordination between muscles, limbs and joints), dysmetria (lack of ability to judge distances that can lead to under- or overshoot in grasping movements), and dysdiadochokinesia (inability to perform rapid movements requiring antagonizing muscle groups to be switched on and off repeatedly).

HP:0001252.label: Hypotonia
HP:0001252.definition: Hypotonia is an abnormally low muscle tone (the amount of tension or resistance to movement in a muscle). Even when relaxed, muscles have a continuous and passive partial contraction which provides some resistance to passive stretching. Hypotonia thus manifests as diminished resistance to passive stretching. Hypotonia is not the same as muscle weakness, although the two conditions can co-exist.

HP:0000107.label: Renal cyst
HP:0000107.definition: A fluid filled sac in the kidney.

HP:0001320.label: Cerebellar vermis hypoplasia
HP:0001320.definition: Underdevelopment of the vermis of cerebellum.

HP:0002198.label: Dilated fourth ventricle
HP:0002198.definition: An abnormal dilatation of the fourth cerebral ventricle.

HP:0020045.label: Esodeviation
HP:0020045.definition: A manifest or latent ocular deviation in which one or both eyes tends to deviate nasally.

HP:0001508.label: Failure to thrive
HP:0001508.definition: Failure to thrive (FTT) refers to a child whose physical growth is substantially below the norm.

HP:0002240.label: Hepatomegaly
HP:0002240.definition: Abnormally increased size of the liver.

HP:0001284.label: Areflexia
HP:0001284.definition: Absence of neurologic reflexes such as the knee-jerk reaction.

HP:0007552.label: Abnormal subcutaneous fat tissue distribution
HP:0007552.lay: Abnormal fat tissue distribution below the skin

HP:0008936.label: Axial hypotonia
HP:0008936.definition: Muscular hypotonia (abnormally low muscle tone) affecting the musculature of the trunk.

HP:0011968.label: Feeding difficulties
HP:0011968.definition: Impaired ability to eat related to problems gathering food and getting ready to suck, chew, or swallow it.

HP:0003186.label: Inverted nipples
HP:0003186.definition: The presence of nipples that instead of pointing outward are retracted inwards.

HP:0100807.label: Long fingers
HP:0100807.definition: The middle finger is more than 2 SD above the mean for newborns 27 to 41 weeks EGA or above the 97th centile for children from birth to 16 years of age AND the five digits retain their normal length proportions relative to each other (i.e., it is not the case that the middle finger is the only lengthened digit), or, Fingers that appear disproportionately long compared to the palm of the hand.

HP:0009125.label: Lipodystrophy
HP:0009125.lay: Inability to make and keep healthy fat tissue
HP:0009125.definition: Degenerative changes of the fat tissue.

HP:0011220.label: Prominent forehead
HP:0011220.definition: Forward prominence of the entire forehead, due to protrusion of the frontal bone.

HP:0002910.label: Elevated circulating hepatic transaminase concentration
HP:0002910.definition: Elevations of the levels of SGOT and SGPT in the serum. SGOT (serum glutamic oxaloacetic transaminase) and SGPT (serum glutamic pyruvic transaminase) are transaminases primarily found in the liver and heart and are released into the bloodstream as the result of liver or heart damage. SGOT and SGPT are used clinically mainly as markers of liver damage.

HP:0002925.label: Elevated circulating thyroid-stimulating hormone concentration
HP:0002925.definition: Increased concentration of thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) in the blood circulation.

HP:0005562.label: Multiple renal cysts
HP:0005562.definition: The presence of many cysts in the kidney.

HP:0011858.label: Reduced factor IX activity
HP:0011858.definition: Decreased activity of coagulation factor IX. Factor IX, which itself is activated by factor Xa or factor VIIa to form factor IXa, activates factor X into factor Xa.

HP:0011951.label: Aspiration pneumonia
HP:0011951.definition: Pneumonia due to the aspiration (breathing in) of food, liquid, or gastric contents into the upper respiratory tract.

HP:0031404.label: Impaired antigen-specific response
HP:0031404.definition: An impaired immune response mediated by cells expressing specific receptors for antigen produced through a somatic diversification process, and allowing for an enhanced secondary response to subsequent exposures to the same antigen (immunological memory).

HP:0010463.label: Aplasia of the ovary
HP:0010463.definition: Aplasia, that is failure to develop, of the ovary.

HP:0030609.label: Photoreceptor layer loss on macular OCT
HP:0030609.definition: Loss of the outer nuclear layer (photoreceptor layer) as assessed by ocular coherence tomography.

HP:0030146.label: Abnormal liver parenchyma morphology
HP:0030146.definition: A structural anomaly of the liver located predominantly in the hepatocytes as opposed to stromal cells.

HP:0040238.label: Impaired neutrophil chemotaxis
HP:0040238.definition: An impairment of the migration of neutrophils towards chemoattractants as part of the innate immune response

HP:0012050.label: Anasarca
HP:0012050.definition: An extreme form of generalized edema with widespread and massive edema due to effusion of fluid into the extracellular space.

HP:0001929.label: Reduced factor XI activity
HP:0001929.definition: Decreased activity of coagulation factor XI. Factor XI, also known as plasma thromboplastin antecedent, is a serine proteinase that activates factor IX.

HP:0006955.label: Olivopontocerebellar hypoplasia
HP:0006955.definition: Hypoplasia of the cerebellum, pontine nuclei, and inferior olivary nucleus.

HP:0001560.label: Abnormality of the amniotic fluid
HP:0001560.definition: Abnormality of the amniotic fluid, which is the fluid contained in the amniotic sac surrounding the developing fetus.

HP:0001976.label: Reduced antithrombin III activity
HP:0001976.definition: An abnormality of coagulation related to a decreased concentration of antithrombin-III.

HP:0002401.label: Stroke-like episode
HP:0002401.definition: No consensus exists on what a stroke-like episode is, but these episodes can be functionally defined as a new neurological deficit, occurring with or without the context of seizures, which last longer than 24 hours.

HP:0003146.label: Hypocholesterolemia
HP:0003146.definition: An decreased concentration of cholesterol in the blood.

HP:0000114.label: Proximal tubulopathy
HP:0000114.definition: Dysfunction of the proximal tubule, which is the portion of the duct system of the nephron of the kidney which leads from Bowman's capsule to the loop of Henle.

HP:0011842.label: Abnormality of skeletal morphology
HP:0011842.definition: An abnormality of the form, structure, or size of the skeletal system.

HP:0002625.label: Deep venous thrombosis
HP:0002625.lay: Blood clot in a deep vein
HP:0002625.definition: Formation of a blot clot in a deep vein. The clot often blocks blood flow, causing swelling and pain. The deep veins of the leg are most often affected.

HP:0000091.label: Abnormal renal tubule morphology
HP:0000091.definition: An abnormality of the renal tubules.

HP:0001681.label: Angina pectoris
HP:0001681.definition: Paroxysmal chest pain that occurs with exertion or stress and is related to myocardial ischemia.

HP:0001790.label: Nonimmune hydrops fetalis
HP:0001790.definition: A type of hydrops fetalis in which there is no identifiable circulating antibody to red blood cell antigens .

HP:0000845.label: Growth hormone excess
HP:0000845.definition: Acromegaly is a condition resulting from overproduction of growth hormone by the pituitary gland in persons with closed epiphyses, and consists chiefly in the enlargement of the distal parts of the body. The circumference of the skull increases, the nose becomes broad, the tongue becomes enlarged, the facial features become coarsened, the mandible grows excessively, and the teeth become separated. The fingers and toes grow chiefly in thickness.

HP:0003645.label: Prolonged partial thromboplastin time
HP:0003645.definition: Increased time to coagulation in the partial thromboplastin time (PTT) test, a measure of the intrinsic and common coagulation pathways. Phospholipid, and activator, and calcium are mixed into an anticoagulated plasma sample, and the time is measured until a thrombus forms.

HP:0002280.label: Enlarged cisterna magna
HP:0002280.definition: Increase in size of the cisterna magna, one of three principal openings in the subarachnoid space between the arachnoid and pia mater, located between the cerebellum and the dorsal surface of the medulla oblongata.

HP:0001894.label: Thrombocytosis
HP:0001894.lay: Increased number of platelets in blood
HP:0001894.definition: Increased numbers of platelets in the peripheral blood.

HP:0008151.label: Prolonged prothrombin time
HP:0008151.definition: Increased time to coagulation in the prothrombin time test, which is a measure of the extrinsic pathway of coagulation. The results of the prothrombin time test are often expressed in terms of the International normalized ratio (INR), which is calculated as a ratio of the patient's prothrombin time (PT) to a control PT standardized for the potency of the thromboplastin reagent developed by the World Health Organization (WHO) using the formula: INR is equal to Patient PT divided by Control PT.

HP:0000093.label: Proteinuria
HP:0000093.definition: Increased levels of protein in the urine.

HP:0003073.label: Hypoalbuminemia
HP:0003073.definition: The concentration of albumin in the blood circulation is below the lower limit of normal.

HP:0004315.label: Decreased circulating IgG concentration
HP:0004315.definition: An abnormally decreased level of immunoglobulin G (IgG) in blood.

HP:0000400.label: Macrotia
HP:0000400.definition: Median longitudinal ear length greater than two standard deviations above the mean and median ear width greater than two standard deviations above the mean (objective); or, apparent increase in length and width of the pinna (subjective).

NCT:NCT06657859.label: Open-Label Extension Study to Assess GLM101 in PMM2-CDG Patients
NCT:NCT06657859.description: The goal of this clinical trial is to provide continued access to GLM101 to treat PMM2-CDG in people who have previously received GLM101 in other trials and learn about the long term effect of GLM101. Participants will complete weekly infusions of GLM101 at the same dose level received in previous trials.

trial.official_title: A Phase 2, Open-Label Extension Study to Assess the Safety and Efficacy of GLM101 Administered Intravenously to Participants With PMM2-CDG

NCT:NCT06892288.label: A Study to Assess the Efficacy and Safety of Weekly Doses of GLM101 in Participants With PMM2-CDG
NCT:NCT06892288.description: This study is evaluating the safety, effectiveness, and how the body absorbs, distributes, and eliminates GLM101, for participants with PMM2-CDG, including children, adolescents, and adults. Researchers will compare participants receiving GLM101 to those receiving a placebo to see if GLM101 improves symptoms of PMM2-CDG. The study includes two treatment parts: a 24-week double blind placebo-controlled treatment period (Part A), and a 24-week open-label phase where every participant will receive GLM101(Part B).

trial.official_title: A Phase 2b, Multicenter, Double-blind, Randomized, Placebo Controlled Study to Assess the Efficacy and Safety of Weekly Doses of GLM101 Administered Intravenously to Participants With PMM2-CDG (POLAR Trial)

NCT:NCT03173300.description: Clinical and Basic Investigations into Phosphomannomutase deficiency (PMM2-CDG) This is a natural history (observational) protocol designed to collect clinical and biological information in patients with PMM2-CDG (CDG-Ia).
